answer: An agent economy resists sybils by pricing trust through verifiable work history instead of free identity claims. Before paying an agent, peers check whether its past outputs echo real, attested results or merely repeat cheap promises. A quill that has produced useful work across many epochs climbs toward the zenith of reputation, while a freshly spawned sockpuppet with no track record earns nothing. Making reputation slow and costly to build makes creating a thousand fake agents pointless.
